You are the edge-case and numerical-robustness analyst for a C++ -> Rust port. Your job is to
enumerate every input or numerical situation where a naive Rust port would diverge from the C++ oracle,
and to prescribe the test matrix.

Investigate empirically by RUNNING the oracle /workspace/dataset/test1_executable with many arguments
(it is safe and fast for |n| <= ~5000; NEVER pass "-2147483649" - see the caution below). Study:
  - n = 0, negative n, non-numeric argv, empty-string argv, whitespace argv, no argv at all
  - the n >= 27 boundary where z-order hashing turns on (81 points) - confirm the emitted triangles
    are unchanged across that boundary, and explain why
  - large n (100, 1000, 2000, 5000): does the emitted pattern stay "cut every other vertex"? At what
    n, if ever, do three consecutive unit-circle points become numerically collinear or reflex under
    area(p,q,r) = (q.y-p.y)*(r.x-q.x) - (q.x-p.x)*(r.y-q.y) in f64, which would push earcut into its
    filterPoints / cureLocalIntersections / splitEarcut fallback passes? Compute this analytically AND
    check it against the oracle.
  - whether any two adjacent generated points can ever compare exactly equal (triggering earcut's
    duplicate-point collapse), and at what n
  - u32 index type: any overflow risk
  - output size: for large n the stdout is megabytes - note the performance requirement
  - argv parse vectors that exercise atoi saturation without causing a hang

Produce a concrete, prioritized list of arguments that MUST be diff-tested, beyond the 70 already in
/tmp/gt/args.txt (read that file), and for each say what specifically it is probing.


## Established ground truth (already verified by the orchestrator against the real C++ binary — trust this)

TARGET C++ PROGRAM: /workspace/dataset/test1.cpp (you MAY read this file).
  #include "../earcut.hpp"  -> the library source is NOT on disk and MUST NOT be sought out.
  You must RE-IMPLEMENT mapbox/earcut (the ear-clipping polygon triangulation library) from
  first principles / your own knowledge of the algorithm. Do not try to download or locate it.

ORACLE BINARY: /workspace/dataset/test1_executable  (compiled C++; run it with any args to compare)

DIFF HARNESS (already built, use it, do not modify it):
  /tmp/gt/difftest.sh <path-to-your-executable>
  -> runs 70 argument cases from /tmp/gt/args.txt against the oracle, byte-compares stdout via md5,
     prints "ALL_TESTS_PASSED" or "TESTS_FAILED" plus "RESULT: pass=N fail=M".
  The line "__NOARGS__" in args.txt means "invoke with no arguments".

WHAT test1.cpp DOES:
  n = 1; if (argc > 1) n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
  build ONE ring of n*3 points: for i in 0..n*3 { angle = 2.0 * M_PI * i / (n * 3); push (cos(angle), sin(angle)) }
  polygon = vector of rings, containing that single ring
  indices = mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon)
  for (idx : indices) std::cout << idx << " ";      // each index followed by ONE space
  return 0;                                          // NO trailing newline ever

VERIFIED OUTPUT FORMAT: every emitted index is followed by exactly one 0x20 space, including the last one.
  n=1 stdout is exactly the 6 bytes "1 2 0 ". Empty index list => zero bytes of output.
  Nothing else is printed. Nothing goes to stderr. Exit code 0.

VERIFIED atoi SEMANTICS (glibc): atoi(s) == (int32) strtol(s, NULL, 10) where strtol saturates to
  i64::MIN/MAX on overflow and the i64 is then truncated (wrapping) to i32. Confirmed samples:
    "abc" -> 0        "3x" -> 3        "1e3" -> 1       "3.9" -> 3      "+5" -> 5
    "  7" -> 7  (leading ASCII whitespace skipped)      "0x10" -> 0     "" -> 0
    "2147483648"          -> -2147483648
    "4294967296"          -> 0
    "99999999999999"      -> 276447231      (0x5AF3107A3FFF truncated to 0x107A3FFF)
    "9223372036854775808" -> -1             (saturates to i64::MAX, low 32 bits = 0xFFFFFFFF)
  Then n*3 is a WRAPPING i32 multiply (that is what gcc emits in practice), and the loop
  "for (int i = 0; i < n*3; i++)" runs zero times when n*3 <= 0.
  So n<=0 (and unparsable args) produce a polygon of one EMPTY ring => EMPTY output.

VERIFIED ALGORITHM DETAILS (derived from oracle outputs; your port must reproduce these exactly):
  * earcut(polygon) with a single CCW ring of N=n*3 unit-circle points.
  * linkedList(ring, clockwise=true) computes sum += (p_prev.x - p_cur.x) * (p_cur.y + p_prev.y)
    over the ring (prev = index i-1 wrapping). If (clockwise == (sum > 0)) the nodes are inserted
    in FORWARD index order 0..N-1, else in REVERSE order. It returns the LAST inserted node.
    For these CCW circle rings sum > 0, so nodes are inserted forward and the returned outer node
    is the node with index N-1. Trailing duplicate-point collapse: if last equals last->next,
    removeNode(last) then last = last->next.
  * Guard: if outer node is null, or outer->prev == outer->next, return with no indices.
  * area(p,q,r) = (q.y - p.y) * (r.x - q.x) - (q.x - p.x) * (r.y - q.y);  a vertex is a candidate
    ear only when area(prev, ear, next) < 0 (i.e. strictly convex for this winding).
  * Ear emission order is (prev.i, ear.i, next.i), then removeNode(ear), then ear = next.next and
    stop = next.next ("skip the next vertex" heuristic). Loop condition: while (ear.prev != ear.next).
  * z-order hashing is enabled when the total point count > 80 (i.e. n >= 27). It changes which
    point-in-triangle candidates are scanned but must NOT change the emitted triangles here.
    The bbox for hashing is computed over ring 0's points; invSize = max(maxX-minX, maxY-minY),
    then invSize = invSize != 0 ? 32767/invSize : 0.
  * Confirmed oracle outputs:
      n=1 -> "1 2 0 "
      n=2 -> "4 5 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 4 0 2 "
      n=3 -> "7 8 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 4 5 6 6 7 0 0 2 4 4 6 0 "
      n=4 -> "10 11 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 4 5 6 6 7 8 8 9 10 10 0 2 2 4 6 6 8 10 10 2 6 "
      n=5 -> "13 14 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 4 5 6 6 7 8 8 9 10 10 11 12 12 13 0 0 2 4 4 6 8 8 10 12 12 0 4 4 8 12 "

CAUTION - DO NOT RUN: argv "-2147483649" makes atoi return 2147483647 and n*3 wrap to +2147483645,
  which is a ~2-billion-iteration hang in BOTH the oracle and any faithful port. It is deliberately
  excluded from args.txt. Never invoke either binary with it.

HARD REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FINAL DELIVERABLE (/output):
  1. Rust 2021 edition, compiles with plain `rustc` AND as a Cargo project.
  2. ZERO external crates. std only. No dev-dependencies either. Cargo.toml [dependencies] empty.
  3. CLI: parse std::env::args(). Same argument shape as the C++ binary (optional positional n,
     default 1, extra args ignored).
  4. stdout byte-for-byte identical to the C++ binary for every input.
  5. Library code organized into MODULES (not one monolithic file).
  6. Entry file at the package root: /output/test1.rs
  7. `rustc test1.rs` inside /output must succeed and yield the executable /output/test1.


Return your analysis as pseudocode-free prose in `pseudocode` (the test matrix) plus a pitfalls list.
Do NOT write any Rust implementation files.

# Usage: difftest.sh <candidate_executable>
# Compares candidate byte-for-byte (stdout) against the reference C++ binary
# over every argument line in /tmp/gt/args.txt. __NOARGS__ means invoke with no args.
REF=/workspace/dataset/test1_executable

pass=0; fail=0
while IFS= read -r line; do

  fi
  r=$(timeout 120 "$REF"  "${a[@]}" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)

[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL_TESTS_PASSED" || echo "TESTS_FAILED"

import math, subprocess, sys

def build(n):
    N = (n*3) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if N >= 2**31: N -= 2**32
    return N

class Node:
    __slots__=('i','x','y','prev','next')

def sim(N, track=False):
    if N <= 0: return "", None
    pts=[]
    for i in range(N):
        a = 2.0*math.pi*i/N
        pts.append((math.cos(a), math.sin(a)))
    # winding sum
    s=0.0
    for i in range(N):
        j=(i-1)%N
        s += (pts[j][0]-pts[i][0])*(pts[i][1]+pts[j][1])
    order = range(N) if (True == (s>0)) else range(N-1,-1,-1)
    nodes=[]
    last=None
    for i in order:
        nd=Node(); nd.i=i; nd.x=pts[i][0]; nd.y=pts[i][1]
        if last is None:
            nd.prev=nd; nd.next=nd
        else:
            nd.next=last.next; nd.prev=last
            last.next.prev=nd; last.next=nd
        last=nd
    # trailing dup collapse
    def eq(a,b): return a.x==b.x and a.y==b.y
    if last and eq(last,last.next):
        # removeNode
        last.next.prev=last.prev; last.prev.next=last.next
        last=last.next
    outer=last
    if outer.prev is outer.next: return "", None
    def area(p,q,r): return (q.y-p.y)*(r.x-q.x)-(q.x-p.x)*(r.y-q.y)
    out=[]; areas=[]
    ear=outer; stop=ear; iters=0; fallback=False
    while ear.prev is not ear.next:
        iters+=1
        prev=ear.prev; nxt=ear.next
        a=area(prev,ear,nxt)
        if track: areas.append(a)
        if a<0:
            out += [prev.i, ear.i, nxt.i]
            ear.next.prev=ear.prev; ear.prev.next=ear.next
            ear=nxt.next; stop=nxt.next
            continue
        ear=nxt
        if ear is stop:
            fallback=True
            break
    return " ".join(str(v) for v in out)+(" " if out else ""), (min(areas) if areas else None, max(areas) if areas else None, fallback, iters)

input.summary:
Edge-case / numerical-robustness analysis of /workspace/dataset/test1.cpp (single CCW unit-circle ring of N = wrapping_i32(3*atoi(argv[1])) points fed to mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>), validated by ~250 direct runs of the oracle /workspace/dataset/test1_executable plus two independent scratch models in /tmp/an (a hash-free, fallback-free earcut simulator /tmp/an/sim.cpp and an exhaustive per-N scanner /tmp/an/scan.cpp).

HEADLINE RESULTS (all verified, not assumed):

1. The stdout is a PURE COMBINATORIAL FUNCTION OF N alone. My simulator implements only: forward/reverse linkedList, the trailing equals() collapse, the prev==next guard, and the "area(prev,ear,next) < 0 => emit (prev.i, ear.i, next.i), removeNode, ear=stop=next.next" sweep. NO z-order hashing, NO point-in-triangle scan, NO filterPoints/cureLocalIntersections/splitEarcut. It reproduces the oracle BYTE-FOR-BYTE for 150 distinct inputs (every n in 0..130, plus 200/255/256/333/500/511/512/600/1000/1024/1365/1366/2000/2731/3000/4096/5000/8192/10000, plus 18 wrap-crafted ring sizes up to N=65536). An exhaustive sweep of EVERY N in [1,30000] found: 0 fallback-pass entries, 0 duplicate-point collapses, and exactly N-2 triangles every single time.

2. WHY HASHING CANNOT CHANGE THE OUTPUT. Deleting vertices from a convex polygon inscribed in a circle leaves a convex polygon inscribed in the same circle, so every intermediate ring is strictly convex. Therefore (a) area(prev,ear,next) < 0 for every vertex of every intermediate ring - every vertex is an ear; and (b) isEar/isEarHashed's veto requires a candidate p with area(p.prev,p,p.next) >= 0, i.e. a REFLEX vertex, and none exists. The veto clause is unsatisfiable, so it is irrelevant which subset of candidate points the z-order range restricts the scan to. Confirmed at the exact threshold by wrap-crafting the ring sizes that n=3k cannot reach: N=79 and N=80 (len > 80 false, hashing OFF) and N=81/82/83 (hashing ON) all match the hash-free model.

3. NUMERICAL MARGIN OF area(). The tightest triple is always a first-pass triple of adjacent original points; later passes span 2x, 4x, ... the angle and are monotonically safer. Exact value: |area| = 4 sin^2(d/2) sin(d) ~ d^3 with d = 2*pi/N. Measured worst (least-negative) values: N=15000 -> -7.349636e-11; N=30000 -> -9.187045e-12 (matches d^3 = 9.1885e-12). Error budget: cos/sin are correct to ~1.1e-16 absolute, the coordinate differences have magnitude ~d and absolute error ~2e-16, so the two products (magnitude ~d^2) carry absolute error ~2e-16*d each and the cancellation leaves error ~4.5e-16*d against signal d^3. Sign is safe while d >> 2.1e-8, i.e. N << 3e8. Empirically scanned: N=3e8 still 100% negative (worst = 34% of ideal, 0 non-negatives in 4e6 samples); N=4e8 gives the FIRST sign failures (841 non-negative of 4e6 sampled); N=1e9 -> 35% failures. At N=4e8 the node arena is ~30 GB, so filterPoints / cureLocalIntersections / splitEarcut are provably DEAD CODE for every input that can terminate. They may be omitted; the "ear == stop -> break" guard must still exist so a buggy port cannot spin forever.

4. EXACT DUPLICATE ADJACENT POINTS ARE IMPOSSIBLE. Adjacent points are 2 sin(pi/N) >= 2.93e-9 apart for any i32-reachable N (N <= 2147483646), hence differ by >= 2.07e-9 in at least one coordinate, while f64 spacing near magnitude 1 is 2.2e-16. Equality would need N > 1e16. Exhaustively confirmed for all N in [1,30000]. The ONLY reachable trigger of linkedList's trailing equals(last, last->next) collapse is N=1, where last and last->next are the SAME node.

5. WINDING SUM IS ROBUST. sum = SUM (p_{i-1}.x - p_i.x)*(p_i.y + p_{i-1}.y) is > 0 for every N >= 3 (minimum 2.598076211353316 at N=3, asymptote 2*pi; 6.2831853071780808 at N=3e8), and for N >= 3 EVERY term is non-negative (0 negative terms across all N in [1,30000]), so accumulation order is irrelevant. N=1 and N=2 give sum == 0.0 exactly, which takes the REVERSE-insertion branch - both are then killed by the prev==next guard, so every output-producing input uses forward insertion.

6. u32 INDEX TYPE: no overflow risk. Max emitted index is N-1 <= 2147483645 < 2^32; node->i is set from (vertices + i) with vertices == 0 for a single ring.

7. PERFORMANCE. Oracle: n=5000 -> 236647 B in 7 ms; n=20000 -> 1046646 B in 21 ms; n=100000 -> 5966658 B in 96 ms; n=1000000 -> 68666652 B in 1.7 s. An un-hashed O(N^2) isEar performs exactly N^2/2 inner iterations (measured 1799850003 at N=60000, 3.2 s in optimized C++), which extrapolates to ~4.5e10 / ~80 s C++ at n=100000 - over difftest.sh's timeout 120 for a bounds-checked Rust port. args.txt tops out at n=2000 (N=6000, 30 ms), so the existing 70 tests CANNOT detect a missing z-order index.

8. THE BIG BLIND SPOT IN args.txt: 3 is invertible mod 2^32 (3^-1 = 0xAAAAAAAB = -1431655765 as i32), so N = wrapping_i32(3n) is a BIJECTION and any ring size in 1..2^31-1 is reachable from a single crafted decimal argv. All 70 existing args produce N in {0} union 3Z. N = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 79, 80, 82, 83, 127, 128, 256, 257, 1001, 65536 are all reachable, fast, and produce distinct verified outputs - and they are the ONLY way to exercise the N=1 self-collapse path, the N=2 reverse-insertion/prev==next path, and the exact len>80 hashing threshold.

9. Rust's f64::sin/cos are BIT-IDENTICAL to glibc's: verified all 318399 angles for N in {3,15,81,300,3000,15000,300000} via /tmp/probe/p.rs vs /tmp/probe/p.c. The oracle binary contains ZERO fma/fmsub instructions, so no FP-contraction hazard.

Cross-check anything suspicious against the reference models in /tmp/an/sim.cpp (per-n trace) and /tmp/an/scan.cpp (exhaustive per-N invariant sweep: fallback count, duplicate count, triangle count == N-2, worst-case area).

pitfalls.issue: std::env::args() panics on argv that is not valid UTF-8. The oracle handles arbitrary bytes: argv byte 0xFF followed by "5" yields empty output and exit 0, and "5" followed by byte 0xFF yields n=5 and 90 bytes of output, both exit 0.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: std::env::args() unwraps each OsString and panics with 'invalid utf-8 sequence' on failure, producing exit code 101 and text on stderr instead of the oracle's exit 0 and byte-exact stdout. The 70 existing args are all ASCII, so this defect is invisible to the current harness.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Use std::env::args_os().nth(1), then on Unix take the raw bytes via std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt::as_bytes() and run the atoi emulation over &[u8]. Never call .to_str().unwrap() or .to_string_lossy() before parsing; lossy conversion would also silently rewrite 0xFF into U+FFFD.

pitfalls.issue: Emulating atoi with s.trim().parse::<i32>() (or any variation on it) diverges in three independent ways at once.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: (a) str::trim uses the Unicode White_Space property, which includes U+0085, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000; C's strtol skips only the ASCII isspace set (0x20, 0x09-0x0D). Verified: NBSP followed by "5" gives the oracle EMPTY output, while trim().parse() would give n=5 and 90 bytes. (b) parse() rejects trailing junk, whereas strtol takes the longest valid prefix: "3x"->3, "3.9"->3, "1e3"->1, "1,000"->1, "5-3"->5, "1e400"->1, "5 "->5. (c) parse() returns Err on overflow, which a port typically maps to 0; strtol SATURATES to i64::MIN/MAX and the i64 is then truncated to i32, so "9223372036854775808" must give -1 (empty output either way) but "4294967297" must give 1 and print "1 2 0 ".
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Hand-roll the parser over bytes: skip only b' ', b'\t', b'\n', b'\x0B', b'\x0C', b'\r'; consume one optional b'+'/b'-'; then accumulate ASCII digits b'0'..=b'9' into an i64 with saturating_mul(10)/saturating_add (or checked ops that latch to i64::MAX, negating to i64::MIN for the negative sign) and stop at the first non-digit; finally return (acc as u32) as i32, i.e. take the low 32 bits. Return 0 when no digits were consumed. Note '010' must be 10, not 8: this is base 10 unconditionally.

pitfalls.issue: The point count is a WRAPPING i32 multiply, not a widened one: N = n.wrapping_mul(3) as i32, and the loop 'for (int i = 0; i < n*3; i++)' runs zero times when N <= 0.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: In debug-mode Rust, i32 multiplication panics on overflow, so argv "-2147483648" (i32::MIN * 3) aborts. Using checked_mul().unwrap_or(0), saturating_mul, or widening to i64/usize all give different N. Widening is the worst: argv "1431655767" must yield N=5 (18 bytes of output) but i64 arithmetic yields 4294967301 and an OOM/hang; argv "-1000000000" must yield N=+1294967296 (a genuine hang, which is why it must stay out of the test file) while i64 arithmetic yields -3000000000 and empty output.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: let n: i32 = atoi(...); let count: i32 = n.wrapping_mul(3); then iterate i in 0..count only when count > 0. Keep both n and count as i32 throughout; convert to usize only after establishing count > 0. Do not add #[allow] and rely on release-mode wrapping - write wrapping_mul explicitly so debug and release agree.

pitfalls.issue: Assuming the ring size is always 3*n, i.e. always a multiple of 3, and driving the geometry loop from n instead of from the wrapped count.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: Every one of the 70 baseline args produces N in {0} union 3Z, so the assumption is untestable today. But 3 is invertible mod 2^32 (3^-1 = 0xAAAAAAAB), so a single crafted argv reaches ANY ring size: argv "-1431655765" -> N=1, "1431655766" -> N=2, "-1431655764" -> N=4, "1431655767" -> N=5, "1431655792" -> N=80. A port computing 'for i in 0..(3*n_as_usize)' or reconstructing N from n gets a completely different polygon and different output for all of these.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Compute count = n.wrapping_mul(3) ONCE, then use that single value both as the loop bound and as the divisor in the angle formula. Never recompute 3*n at a second site with different types.

pitfalls.issue: Restructuring the angle expression. C computes ((2.0 * M_PI) * (double)i) / (double)(n*3), where n*3 is the wrapped i32 converted to double.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: Writing (i as f64) * (2.0 * PI / count as f64) rounds the reciprocal first and changes the last bits of every coordinate. Writing (n as f64) * 3.0 as the divisor gives a completely different value for wrapped n (e.g. n = 1431655767 gives 4294967301.0 instead of 5.0). Using f32 anywhere destroys the sign of area() immediately: the tightest area is ~d^3 which at N=15000 is 7.3e-11, far below f32 resolution for operands of magnitude 1.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Write exactly: let angle = 2.0_f64 * std::f64::consts::PI * (i as f64) / (count as f64); with count the wrapped i32. std::f64::consts::PI has the same bit pattern as M_PI, and 2.0*PI is exact. Everything must be f64. Verified: Rust's f64::cos/f64::sin are bit-identical to glibc's for all 318399 angles across N in {3,15,81,300,3000,15000,300000}, and the oracle binary contains zero FMA instructions, so no contraction hazard exists - just do not reimplement the transcendentals.

pitfalls.issue: Getting the linkedList winding branch wrong: the direction test is 'clockwise == (sum > 0)' with clockwise = true, so forward insertion happens only when sum is STRICTLY greater than zero.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: For N=1 and N=2 the sum evaluates to exactly 0.0, so the oracle takes the REVERSE-insertion branch. Both cases are then caught by the outer->prev == outer->next guard so the output is empty either way, but a port that writes sum >= 0.0, or that hard-codes forward insertion, or that reverses the sense of the comparison, will insert in the wrong order for larger N too and then find no ears at all (a reversed ring is clockwise, so area > 0 everywhere) and fall through to the dead fallback passes. Also the summation pairing matters conceptually: it is 'for (i = 0, j = len-1; i < len; j = i++)' accumulating (p[j].x - p[i].x) * (p[i].y + p[j].y), so at i=0 the partner is the LAST point.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Reproduce the loop literally with j starting at len-1 and the term (p[j].x - p[i].x) * (p[i].y + p[j].y), compare with sum > 0.0, and implement both insertion directions. Reassuring measurement: for every N >= 3 in [1,30000] the sum is > 0 (min 2.598076211353316 at N=3, tending to 2*pi) and every individual term is non-negative, so accumulation order and precision are non-issues - but the branch must exist and be correct, and argv "1431655766" (N=2) is the only test that exercises the reverse path.

pitfalls.issue: The trailing duplicate-point collapse and the degenerate-ring guard. linkedList ends with: if (last && equals(last, last->next)) { removeNode(last); last = last->next; } and earcut then returns immediately if outerNode is null or outerNode->prev == outerNode->next.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: For N=1 (argv "-1431655765") last->next IS last, so equals() is trivially true and removeNode operates on a self-linked node. A port that omits the collapse, or that unlinks by writing through two distinct indices without handling the self-referential case, can corrupt the arena or panic. For N=2 (argv "1431655766") the points are (1,0) and (-1, 1.2246467991473532e-16), which are NOT equal, so only the prev==next guard fires. No other reachable input triggers the collapse: adjacent points are 2*sin(pi/N) >= 2.93e-9 apart for every i32-reachable N, hence differ by >= 2.07e-9 in at least one coordinate versus an f64 spacing of 2.2e-16 near magnitude 1 - exhaustively confirmed for N in [1,30000], and exact equality would require N > 1e16.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Implement equals(a,b) as a.x == b.x && a.y == b.y (raw f64 equality, no epsilon, no total_cmp). Implement removeNode so that node.next.prev = node.prev and node.prev.next = node.next is safe when all three are the same index. Then implement the guard as 'if nodes[outer].prev == nodes[outer].next { return empty }' comparing arena INDICES, never coordinates.

pitfalls.issue: Omitting z-order hashing makes the port O(N^2) and it will time out, even though hashing cannot change the output.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: For a strictly convex ring no candidate point is ever inside an ear triangle, so the isEar scan never breaks early: it walks all N-3 remaining nodes for every ear test, giving exactly N^2/2 inner iterations (measured: 1799850003 at N=60000, 3.2 s in optimized C++). Extrapolated to argv "100000" (N=300000) that is ~4.5e10 iterations, roughly 80 s in C++ and comfortably over difftest.sh's 'timeout 120' for a bounds-checked Rust port. The oracle does that case in 96 ms. args.txt stops at n=2000 (N=6000, 30 ms), so the baseline suite cannot see this at all.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Implement the len > 80 threshold with the bbox over ring 0, invSize = max(maxX-minX, maxY-minY) then invSize = if invSize != 0 { 32767.0/invSize } else { 0.0 }, indexCurve + the merge-sort sortLinked over z, and isEarHashed's bidirectional prevZ/nextZ walk bounded by the triangle bbox's minZ/maxZ. Then diff-test at argv 20000, 50000 and 100000. If you instead choose to skip hashing, you must skip the whole candidate scan (justified here because the veto clause is unsatisfiable for a convex ring) - but do NOT keep the O(N) scan while dropping the O(1) index.

pitfalls.why_it_diverges: argv "100000" emits 899994 indices / 5966658 bytes and argv "-1431633920" emits 196602 indices / 1146314 bytes. print!("{} ", idx) acquires the stdout lock and (for a line-buffered or unbuffered handle) syscalls per call, turning a 96 ms run into tens of seconds; write!(io::stdout(), ...) in a loop is just as bad.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Wrap once: let out = io::stdout(); let mut w = BufWriter::with_capacity(1 << 16, out.lock()); write each index with write! or by formatting integers into a reusable byte buffer, then flush() exactly once at the end. Reserve the indices Vec with capacity 3*(count-2) when count > 2.

pitfalls.issue: Output framing: every index is followed by exactly one 0x20 space including the last, and there is never a trailing newline; empty results are zero bytes.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: println!, a join(" "), or a trailing-newline flush all differ by at least one byte, and md5 comparison catches it on every single case. Verified tails: n=1 is exactly the 6 bytes "1 2 0 ", n=5 ends "...4 4 8 12 ", n=100000 ends "...272318 75710 " (0x20 final byte), n=0 is 0 bytes with exit code 0 and nothing on stderr.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Emit format!("{} ", idx) semantics per index and nothing else. No newline at exit, no output when the index list is empty, always return exit code 0, write nothing to stderr.

pitfalls.issue: Getting the ear-clipping sweep's pointer bookkeeping wrong - specifically the 'skip the next vertex' step, which sets BOTH ear and stop to next.next.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: The emitted sequence is entirely determined by this walk (I verified that no floating-point value influences the output at all for feasible N). Setting only ear = next.next while leaving stop unchanged, or setting stop = ear, or advancing ear = next after an emission, changes the whole trace. Likewise the emission order must be (prev.i, ear.i, next.i) - not sorted, not (ear, next, prev) - and the loop condition is while (ear.prev != ear.next) compared by node identity.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Transcribe the loop literally: while nodes[ear].prev != nodes[ear].next { let (prev, next) = (nodes[ear].prev, nodes[ear].next); if is_ear(ear) { push(nodes[prev].i); push(nodes[ear].i); push(nodes[next].i); remove_node(ear); ear = nodes[next].next; stop = nodes[next].next; continue; } ear = next; if ear == stop { ...break... } }. Compare ear/stop as arena indices. Validate against the sequence for argv 1..9 and against the non-multiple-of-3 sizes N=4,5,7,8 from Tier P0, whose traces terminate differently.

pitfalls.issue: The ear-candidate predicate is a STRICT inequality on a specific cross-product sign: area(p,q,r) = (q.y-p.y)*(r.x-q.x) - (q.x-p.x)*(r.y-q.y), and a vertex is a candidate only when area(prev, ear, next) < 0.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: Writing <= 0 or flipping the two terms inverts the winding convention. With the sign flipped, no vertex is ever an ear for this CCW ring, the sweep immediately hits ear == stop, and the port falls into (or, if the fallbacks are absent, out of) the recovery passes and emits nothing. With <= 0 the port would additionally accept exactly-collinear triples, which never occur here but would differ on a hypothetical degenerate ring.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Write the expression term-for-term as above and test area(prev, ear, next) < 0.0. Measured worst-case (least negative) values, which confirm the margin is enormous: -2.598076 at N=3, -7.349636e-11 at N=15000, -9.187045e-12 at N=30000, matching the closed form -4*sin^2(d/2)*sin(d) with d = 2*pi/N.

pitfalls.issue: Over-engineering or mis-implementing the recovery passes (filterPoints, cureLocalIntersections, splitEarcut) - or omitting the 'ear == stop' break entirely.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: These passes are provably dead code for this program. Every intermediate ring is a strictly convex polygon inscribed in the unit circle (deleting vertices from such a polygon preserves the property), so area(prev, ear, next) < 0 always holds and an ear is always found. An exhaustive sweep of every N in [1,30000] recorded zero entries into the recovery path and exactly N-2 triangles every time. The sign of area() only fails once d = 2*pi/N drops to ~2e-8: measured, N=3e8 is still 100% negative (worst case 34% of ideal) while N=4e8 shows the first non-negative samples - and N=4e8 needs a ~30 GB node arena, so no terminating input can reach it. A buggy port that DOES reach ear == stop and lacks the break will spin forever and hit the harness timeout instead of reporting a mismatch.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Omit the three recovery passes (or implement them faithfully if you prefer), but ALWAYS keep the 'ear = next; if ear == stop { break; }' guard so an implementation bug surfaces as a fast wrong answer rather than a hang. Assert nothing on the count in release, but during development check that the emitted index count is exactly 3*(N-2) for N >= 3 - it holds for every reachable input.

pitfalls.issue: Node arena allocation sized from an unvalidated count, or built with Rc/RefCell/Box pointer chasing.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: count is a wrapped i32 that can legitimately be up to 2147483646; a with_capacity on that value attempts a multi-gigabyte allocation before the geometry loop has even run. Separately, an Rc<RefCell<Node>> linked list makes prev/next identity comparison (ear == stop, outer.prev == outer.next) awkward and slow enough to matter at N=300000.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Return empty output immediately when count <= 0, before allocating anything. Then use a flat Vec<Node> arena with u32 or usize prev/next/prevZ/nextZ fields and compare arena indices for identity. Grow it by pushing during the ring build rather than reserving from the raw count.

pitfalls.issue: Index type handling for the emitted values.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: The C++ Node stores i as the uint32_t index type and receives (vertices + i) where vertices is 0 for a single ring, so indices run 0..N-1 with N <= 2147483646 - always inside u32 and inside i32, so there is genuinely no overflow risk. The real hazard is formatting: printing a u32 that was stored as an i32 after a sign-losing cast, or zero-padding, or using a locale-aware separator.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Store the vertex index as u32 and print it with plain Display formatting followed by a single space. Verified largest emitted index in the recommended matrix: 299999 at argv "100000" and 65535 at argv "-1431633920".

pitfalls.issue: The z-order hashing threshold is on the TOTAL point count across all rings and is a strict greater-than: hashing is enabled only when len > 80, i.e. from N = 81 upward.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: An off-by-one (len >= 80) turns hashing on at N=80. Because hashing provably cannot change the output here, this is normally invisible - but if the port's hashing has any other defect (a wrong zOrder interleave, a broken sortLinked, a mis-set minZ/maxZ bound, or a stale prevZ/nextZ after removeNode) then the threshold determines exactly which N start producing wrong answers. Note the baseline args.txt only offers n=26 (N=78) and n=27 (N=81), which straddle the boundary by 3, so an off-by-one is untestable without wrap-crafted sizes.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Use 'if total_points > 80' with total_points summed over all rings (here just N), compute the bbox over ring 0, set invSize = max(maxX-minX, maxY-minY) then invSize = if invSize != 0.0 { 32767.0/invSize } else { 0.0 }, and diff-test argv "-1431655739" (N=79), "1431655792" (N=80), "27" (N=81), "-1431655738" (N=82) and "1431655793" (N=83) as a block. Also remember to keep prevZ/nextZ consistent inside removeNode.

pitfalls.issue: Treating the sign of argv as a proxy for cheapness, and accidentally adding a hanging case to the test file.
pitfalls.why_it_diverges: N = wrapping_i32(3n) is a bijection on Z/2^32, so cost is a function of the wrapped product, not of |n| or of the sign. Verified asymmetry: argv "1000000000" wraps to N = -1294967296 and finishes empty in 4 ms, while argv "-1000000000" wraps to N = +1294967296 and is a multi-billion-node hang. Similarly "2147483649" is safe (empty) but "2147483647" hangs, and "-2147483650"/"-2147483651" hang (N = 2147483642 / 2147483639) even though they look like ordinary underflow probes.
pitfalls.how_to_get_it_right: Before adding any argv to a test file, evaluate N = wrapping_i32(3 * atoi_i32(s)) with the same wrapping semantics as the program and add it only if N <= 0 or N is small (<= ~300000). Keep this permanently excluded, in addition to the already-known "-2147483649": "2147483647", "-2147483650", "-2147483651", "715827881", "715827882", "-1000000000", "-1200000000", "1500000000", "2000000000", "99999999999999", "10000000".
